newsitem.title: SOMALIA: Ten killed in fighting between rival Somali factions.
newsitem.headline: Ten killed in fighting between rival Somali factions.

text.p: At least 10 people were killed and 17 wounded in heavy fighting between rival Somali factions at Jilib town and Haramka village, 460 km (290 miles) south of Mogadishu, on Saturday, travellers from the area reported on Sunday.
They said people had fled from their homes, many of which were set ablaze during the fighting.
According to witnesses, the fighting was between supporters of the Shikhal and Gale'el clans, using heavy machine-guns and armoured battlewagons.
Colonel Yusuf Mugdi, a Gaje'el militia leader, was quoted as saying the rival clan had seized control of Jilib, but were later driven out in fierce fighting.
The Shikhal militia normally support the self-styled Somali government now led by Hussein Farah Aideed, while the Gaje'el have remained independent of the main warlords.
Reports from the area on Sunday said the situation was still tense, and there was no sign of peace negotiations between the rival groups.
